title: Dynamic density reflow causing chart tooltip clipping and button hit-area regressions on Safari/iOS and Firefox
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: Multiple UI Kit components (density toggle, virtualized lists/tables, chart tooltips, and compact buttons) are exhibiting visual regressions in Safari on iOS and desktop Safari, and in several Firefox desktop builds. Common symptoms: chart tooltip clipping when density changes, virtualized list row reflow that causes sticky header jitter, and reduced/touch-unfriendly button hit areas in compact mode. These appear after a recent token scale change and virtualized-list refactor. This ticket scopes cross-browser reproduction, triage, and design guidance for fixes; engineering fixes will be tracked as follow-ups.
reproduction_steps: Open staging UI Kit demo page (compact-density view) on iPhone 12 / iOS 16 Safari and on macOS Safari 16
Navigate to Charts > Line + Tooltip example with large data set and enable 'Compact density' toggle
Scroll the surrounding virtualized list rapidly to trigger lazy row rendering while hovering (desktop) or tapping (mobile) chart points; observe tooltip clipping or unexpected truncation
On Firefox desktop, open the same demo and toggle density; observe button focus ring offset and table row boundary misalignment when virtualization recycles rows
Record console logs and take slow-motion screen capture for mobile; note any CSS transform or position changes during reflow
triage_notes: Reproducible reliably on Safari (iOS + macOS) and Firefox Nightly; Chrome appears unaffected. Regression introduced after token scale change v2 (token-density-2026) plus virtualization refactor (ENG-4631). Hypothesis: density token changes alter calculated heights; virtualization uses fractional pixels and transforms which combined with -webkit-overflow-scrolling and matrix transforms produce rounding errors causing tooltip container to be clipped by overflow:hidden parents. Button hit areas appear reduced because compact button padding tokens were tightened and hitbox rules rely on line-height assumptions.
decisions: 1) Prefer a compatibility shim that forces integer pixel heights for virtualized rows on WebKit/Firefox until kernel fix is implemented. 2) Revert token values that reduce touch target below 44px min on mobile; keep visual compactness but preserve padding via pseudo-element hit area expansion. 3) Chart tooltip container to be promoted out of overflow stack (use portal) with safe max-width and pointer-following behavior as interim.
action_items: Design: provide exact token rollback values and hit-area pseudo-element spec (Maya)
Engineering: implement integer-pixel virtualization option and tooltip portal (ENG-4631, assigned)
QA: add cross-browser e2e scenario in Playwright covering density toggle + virtualization + tooltip (add to regression suite)
Docs: update component migration notes for compact density changes and known Safari/Firefox quirks
Schedule: coordinate a small canary release for ui-kit-2026.03 with fixes behind feature flags
notes:
Acceptance criteria:
- Tooltip no longer clips across Safari iOS/macOS and Firefox when density is toggled while virtualized lists are rendering.
- Compact buttons maintain >=44px touch target on mobile (or equivalent hit-area expansion) while visual density retained.
- No new layout jitter introduced on Chrome.
- Regression tests added to Playwright and run in CI.
Post-mortem: include timeline of token change and virtualization refactor, link to ENG patch and PRs.
